image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Approach above the live red hub with open fingers, leveling the hand; estimate hub location from the calibrated head view.
Descend around the red hub, correcting the small lateral offset seen in the wrist view; keep fingers open.
Settle the pads around the hub and close gradually to grasp, then inspect contact before lifting.
Lift the gripped gear clear of the table and verify that it stays between the pads.
Carry the visibly retained gear toward the empty base spindle at clearance height; refine alignment from the next views.
Fine-align laterally over the spindle using the wrist gear-center offset, while lowering toward the base.
Lower the retained red gear vertically onto the aligned spindle, stopping just above expected seating height to inspect engagement.
The gear tilted during insertion, suggesting a spindle alignment error. Withdraw vertically while retaining it before correcting alignment.
The gear leveled after withdrawal. Correct the spindle approach a few millimeters and retry insertion cautiously, watching for tilt.
Contact still distorts the grasp. Back off and shift toward the spindle's calibrated image location before another slow seating attempt.
Try the corrected spindle alignment with a slow descent and a slight tooth-aligning turn; monitor gear tilt and pad contact.
Withdraw from tilted contact and shift toward the spindle before retrying insertion. Rejected commands made no motion; corrected all rotation entries.
Test the revised alignment with a slow 10 mm descent and small tooth-alignment rotation; inspect whether the gear seats or tilts.
Corrected invalid rotation entry; no prior motion occurred. Lift and move aside to expose the spindle for fresh visual alignment.
Use the newly exposed spindle top and base to correct the larger x alignment error; approach vertically after centering above it.
The corrected approach is level above the visible spindle. Lower slowly with a submillimeter lateral correction, checking for seating rather than renewed tilt.
The gear is tilting rather than seating. Withdraw and expose the spindle again to measure its alignment before further insertion.
Recenter above the exposed spindle using both its top and base projections; keep ample clearance before testing insertion.
Lower vertically at the newly measured spindle center, keeping the gear retained and checking alignment before final seating.
The gear is nearly level at this approach. Continue a shallow descent with a small tooth-aligning turn, watching for seating or renewed tilt.
Relieve the contact slightly, correct the small hub-to-spindle offset, then try a shallow descent with tooth-aligning rotation.
Back off the tilted contact and try a corrected center between previous approaches, accounting for the live grasp offset and base displacement.
Relieve contact, refine the spindle center from its base projection, and relax the fingers slightly so the gear can settle rather than remain wedged in a tilted grasp.
Release the red gear over the spindle and allow it to settle without pad constraint; lift slightly to inspect its support and alignment.
Move the open fingers clear and allow the released gear to settle so its support and spindle alignment are visible.
The released gear is perched on the spindle, not seated. Regrasp its hub firmly at this raised position before correcting the bore alignment.
Lift the regrasped gear clear and expose the spindle. Check whether the hub stays level before another alignment attempt.
The regrasp holds the gear tilted. Return to the clear table area to set it flat and recover a level hub grasp before insertion.
Set the tilted gear down in the clear table area and release it to settle flat before recovering a centered grasp.
Recenter the open hand over the now-flat red hub using its head projection, restore a level grasp orientation, and descend to hub height.
Correct the hub offset visible in the wrist image before closing around the level hub; avoid lifting until contact is centered.
Lift the newly centered, level grasp and approach beside the base, leaving the spindle visible for a more precise alignment.
Corrected the invalid rotation entry; no motion occurred. Bring the level gear above the visually estimated spindle center at clearance height.
With the recovered level grasp, make a small spindle-center correction and approach its top slowly, before deeper insertion.
Correct the small lateral bore offset and gently turn while lowering, allowing tooth alignment rather than forcing a straight insertion.
Withdraw and expose the spindle for fresh visual alignment. All rotation increments are zero; previous rejected commands made no motion.
Return the level gear above the exposed spindle using a revised center between prior approaches, then stop near first contact for a controlled alignment search.
Search toward smaller x at shallow contact, accounting for the gear's offset within the grasp; use only slight descent and rotation.
Clear the tilted contact and expose the peg. Restore the wrist heading to measure the peg relative to the retained gear before a localized alignment search.
Approach a revised bore center between the previous offsets, using the exposed spindle projection. Keep clearance for a controlled rotational seating attempt.
